newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan more tolerant of US growth -- BusinessWeek.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan more tolerant of US growth -- BusinessWeek.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan appears more tolerant of faster growth and lower unemployment than the central bank has been in the past, according to an article in the July 14 BusinessWeek.

"There is a sense in which (Greenspan) is the extreme dove," the story quoted a Fed source as saying. "He has been willing to let the economy run tighter than what a lot of people have been comfortable with."
But Greenspan has told associates that his core values have not changed since President Ronald Reagan appointed him Fed chief in 1987, according to the article.
The economy, however, has evolved in the face of increased global competition that has helped to moderate U.S. wage growth, it said.
Greenspan believes the U.S. economy is going through a dramatic change in productivity, and he thinks statistical aberrations understate efficiency increases, the article said.
Because productivity gains should boost corporate profits, the central bank chairman has also taken a more benevolent view of the rising stock market, it said.
Greenspan now has more faith that shifts in the financial markets can perform much of the Fed's job of regulating the economy, it said.
Greenspan has not given an on-the-record interview in six years, according to BusinessWeek, and was not quoted directly in the article.
